# Kalumba et al. (2021) PTFs for Zambezi River Basin soil hydraulic properties.

## Source

Kalumba, M., Bamps, B., Nyambe, I., Dondeyne, S., & Van Orshoven, J. (2021). Development and functional evaluation of pedotransfer functions for soil hydraulic properties for the Zambezi River Basin. European Journal of Soil Science, 72(4), 1559-1574.

[DOI: 10.1111/ejss.13077](https://doi.org/10.1111/ejss.13077)

## Scope

**Territory:** Zambezi River Basin, with field measurements from the Upper Mulungushi sub-basin.

**Dataset:** 631 soil samples: 329 Africa Soil Profiles observations and 302 Upper Mulungushi observations; target-specific sample availability is documented below.

## Functions

### `calc_ptf_kalumba2021_mlr_pf00`

Estimate volumetric water content at pf 0.0 with the Kalumba et al. MLR PTF.

**Status:** `implemented`

**Prediction target:** Volumetric water content at pF 0.0.

**Models:** $h(\theta)$ — Multiple linear regression point estimate at pF 0.0.

#### Inputs

| Name | Type | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `elevation` | `number` | m | 81 <= value <= 1924 | Topographic elevation of the soil profile site. |
| `sand` | `number` | fraction | 0.032 <= value <= 0.973 | Sand fraction used as a PTF input. |
| `silt` | `number` | fraction | 0.047 <= value <= 0.786 | Silt fraction used as a PTF input. |
| `stoniness` | `number` | fraction | 0 <= value <= 0.85 | Stoniness fraction under the reviewed Table 4 scale interpretation. |
| `nitrogen` | `number` | % | 0 <= value <= 0.366 | Soil nitrogen content in percentage points. |
| `electrical_conductivity` | `number` | dS/m | 0.001 <= value <= 0.090 | Soil electrical conductivity. |
| `ph` | `number` | 1 | 4.98 <= value <= 8.50 | Soil pH measured in a 1:5 soil-to-water suspension. |
| `bulk_density` | `number` | g/cm^3 | 0.83 <= value <= 2.04 | Soil bulk density. |

#### Outputs

| Name | Unit | Domain | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `water_content_pf00` | fractions | 0 <= value <= 1 | Volumetric water content at pF 0.0. |

!!! note

    Table 4 publishes the complete MLR equation; the target dataset is 302 Upper Mulungushi observations.

!!! warning

    Developed for Zambezi River Basin soils; the Table 1 ranges are marginal and do not define a joint Cartesian applicability domain.
